name: relu
summary: ReLU elementwise: out = max(in, 0). Any-rank contiguous tensors are flattened to 1D numel. Variants: f32 naive, f16 naive, f16 half2(vec2) fastpath when numel even and pointers 4B aligned. AttrBlob is ignored (no attrs).
contract: - I and O must have same rank and identical shape (any-rank).
- Both I and O must be contiguous (checked via strides; last stride==1 and stride[i]==shape[i+1]*stride[i+1]).
- numel(I) == numel(O) must satisfy 0 < numel <= INT_MAX (kernel uses int N).
abi: Dispatcher may pass any attr; kernel ignores it.
notes: Any-rank flatten is logical only; kernel assumes linear contiguous memory.
f16 vec2 path requires numel even and 4B alignment for in/out pointers.

variants.name: relu_f16_vec2_half2
variants.notes: Processes __half2 lanes; computes out = max(in, 0) via __hmax2.

suites.name: basic_correctness
suites.desc: Compare output against reference max(x,0) over various shapes and dtypes.

suites.name: half2_gating
suites.desc: Validate vec2 selection logic and fallback behavior.

cases.notes: Make output pointer misaligned to break 4B alignment.
Use a strided view where stride[last]!=1.

experiments.title: half2 fastpath
experiments.change: Use __half2 + __hmax2 for f16 when numel even and 4B aligned.
experiments.why: Vectorize memory ops and reduce instruction count.
experiments.hypothesis: Higher bandwidth utilization on memory-bound ReLU.
experiments.next: Add LDG.128 vectorization (half8) for larger alignment if needed.

experiments.title: Any-rank via stride-checked contiguity
experiments.change: Accept arbitrary rank by flattening numel, but require strict contiguous strides.
experiments.why: Maximize reuse for elementwise ops with minimal specialization.
experiments.hypothesis: Simplifies lowering and avoids shape-specific kernels.
experiments.next: Optional: allow TensorDesc.contiguous shortcut if guaranteed correct.

measurements.notes: Effective bytes ~= read+write = numel*2B*2. Compare naive vs vec2.
